text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ministerial privatisation group, chaired by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, will today discuss a new system for reforming 50 troubled public-sector companies. The system includes offering these companies to the private sector to take part in managing them and sharing the profits.

- Cabinet Affairs Minister Talaat Hammad said after a meeting of the ministerial group on investment that the government has started to study all the instructions given by President Hosni Mubarak at his meeting with media people on Saturday. He said the main instruction was to provide medical treatment for the poor at the expense of the state.

- President Mubarak is expected to received Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara this morning. They are bringing a message for Mubarak from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.

- The chairman of the Capital Market Authority, Abdelhamid Ibrahim, announced that the state has decided to exempt from taxation financing activities that promote direct investment in the stock exchange. The activities include subscription to equity, which will have a temporary exemption, as well as underwriting and financing leasing.

- Mubarak's two sons, Alaa and Gamal, through lawyer Raga'i Atiya, have complained to public prosecutor Raga el-Arabi about advertisments in the newspaper Asharq al-Awsat and the magazine al-Jadida. Their complaint says the advertisements contain false allegations.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz held talks in Israel as part of consultations with Israel and the Palestinians on breaking the deadlock in the Middle East peace process.

- The results of last year's national census will be released today. The head of the government's statistics agency said the results give a real indication of the level of unemployment and of temporary emigration for work abroad.
- The Damascus Declaration states will hold their next meeting in Syria on June 25 at the request of Egypt.

- Egypt has reiterated the need to eradicate nuclear weapons regionally and globally according to a fixed timetable, said ambassador Munir Zahran, Egypt's permanent representative at the United Nations in Geneva.

- The legislative committee of parliament has agreed to lift the parliamentary immunity of Mustafa el-Said, the chairman of the economic committee and a former minister. Said faces charges of breach of trust in connection with cheques for 100,000 pounds ($29,000). Said disputed the decision and asked for more time to justify his position.
